action: Local governments: keep an offline copy of resident-service procedures and confirm you can cut the network quickly and work on paper. Residents of Chambourcy: be alert to phishing that mentions the town hall.
exec: A small municipality had to switch its IT off and fall back to paper, a reminder that local-government resilience planning matters for service continuity.
impact: IT network shut down as a precaution; municipal services largely on paper with slower processing; reception, phone and website still working.
plain: The town hall of Chambourcy, near Paris, was hit by a cyberattack over the weekend of November 7-8 and turned off its network. Services are mostly handled on paper and take longer.
summary: The town hall of Chambourcy (Yvelines) reported a cyberattack over the weekend of 7-8 November and shut its IT network as a precaution. Most services moved to paper; in-person reception, phone and website work normally and email replies are slower. It filed a complaint and informed the CNIL. It has not said who is behind the attack or how much data is affected.
title: Chambourcy town hall in France hit by cyberattack, services moved to paper

validation.note: Single regional outlet; the town hall's own notice was not read.
